simple.meaning: יַצַע (yatsaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to strew as a surface.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Esther, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Esther 4:3. The surrounding contexts include commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יַצַע (H3331) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יַצַע (yatsaʻ) / H3331 is traced through Esther 4:3, Psalms 139:8, Isaiah 14:11, Isaiah 58:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3331. yatsa [ יָצַע ] verb Hiph`il lay, spread , late (Ges § 71 ; Aramaic יְצַע Pa`el, Aph`el id. , also expound , 'auslegen;' Arabic is put or lay (down, on a place, etc.), but = Aramaic ע ) — Hiph`il Imperfect יַצִּיעַ Isa 58:5 ; אַצִּ֫יעָה Psa 139:8 ; lay, spread out , followed by accusative ואפר שׂק Isa 58:5 ; שׁאול Psa 139:8 if I spread out Sh®°ôl (as my couch). Hoph`al Imperfect יֻצַּע ( Pu`al Perfect De Di and others) be laid, spread ; subject ואפר שׂק Est 4:3 ; subject רִמָּה worm, as couch for king of Babylon Isa 14:11 .

occurrences.englishText: In every province, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
If I ascend up into heaven, you are there.
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol,† Sheol is the place of the dead. with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.
Is this the fast that I have chosen?
